correctness.rationale: Given Pi(i)=i, the remaining bijection is uniform. Nonincident comparisons stay fair; an incident comparison has conditional success probability (n-i)/(n-1) if its right endpoint is i, and (i-1)/(n-1) if its left endpoint is i. Subtracting 1/2 and multiplying by 1/n proves the basis identities and hence the real-weight formula, also at n=2. Setting weights to one gives the negative square and summing it gives -(n+1)/6. The fixed-point factorial moments give variance one; the independent insertion ranks of a uniform permutation give inversion variance n(n-1)(2n+5)/72. These yield the stated correlation and asymptotic. Independent replay: python3 -I -B /workspace/audit_replays/frozen_math.py 1, with 322 exact basis-weight tests plus marginal variances and aggregate covariance for n=2 through 7.
residual_risks: The result concerns first conditional moments, not the full conditional law or independence at the central site.
